Suhopolje Jewish Section within Municipal Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Suhopolje, Croatia

Not demolished. A settlement called Szentendre stood on the site of modern Suhopolje as early as 1334, presumably destroyed by Ottoman invasion in 1532, with the area left nearly uninhabited until the end of Ottoman rule in 1684; the 19th century brought rapid growth. Suhopolje's Jews belonged to the nearby Virovitica community, numbering 23 before WWII and dwindling to just 4 by 1947. This cemetery, built in the 19th century within the grounds of a larger Catholic cemetery though kept separate, holds inscriptions in Hungarian, Croatian, Hebrew, and German; about 10-15 monuments remained as of a 2009 count, with tombstones ranging from 1914 to as late as 1949.
